title: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer using chem-bioinformatics-driven engineering of exosomal cargo-vehicle for telmisartan and pioglitazone targeted-delivery.
authors: Hamdy, Nadia M; Sanad, Eman F; Kassab, Shaymaa E; Essam, Merhan; Guirguis, Monica A; Basalious, Emad B; Sultan, Ahmed S
one_liner_zh: 该文聚焦PPARG转录因子激动剂药物递送治疗肺癌，虽涉及分子对接与MD，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: The activation of the PPARG transcription factor is linked to reduced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) growth. Bioinformatics, cheminformatics, and molecular docking/dynamics studies assessing pioglitazone and telmisartan as repurposed PPARG agonists for treating NSCLC with a targeted delivery system was done. Bioinformatics confirmed that the expression of the PPARG gene can predict outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma and is related to immune cells present in the tumor. Cheminformatics data showed that pioglitazone and telmisartan have a strong attraction to the PPARG receptor, with good efficiency as ligands. Both drugs were found to be lipophilic, suggesting compatibility with a targeted delivery formulation that may include albumin. Further cheminformatics predictions highlighted systemic toxicity values and the need for targeted delivery to minimize toxic side effects. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations showed that the telmisartan-MyoVc cargo domain complex was strong and stable during an 18 ns simulation period. Bioinformatics and cheminformatics data support pioglitazone and telmisartan as promising repurposed drugs for LUAC, highlighting their lipophilicity and compatibility with exosomal components like albumin. Cheminformatics also pointed out potential off-target effects and hepatotoxicity, emphasizing the importance of exosomal targeted delivery. Molecular docking and MD simulations confirmed the affinity and stability of drug-exosomal vehicle complexes. The proposed engineering of exosomal cargo for targeted delivery of these drugs to lung cells could enhance NSCLC treatment and address drug resistance while minimizing systemic toxicity.
abstract_zh: PPARG转录因子的激活与非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）生长减少相关。本研究进行了生物信息学、化学信息学以及分子对接/动力学研究，评估吡格列酮和替米沙坦作为重新定位的PPARG激动剂，用于通过靶向递送系统治疗NSCLC。生物信息学证实，PPARG基因的表达可预测肺腺癌的预后，并与肿瘤中存在的免疫细胞相关。化学信息学数据显示，吡格列酮和替米沙坦对PPARG受体具有强吸引力，作为配体表现出良好的效率。两种药物均被发现具有亲脂性，提示其与可能包含白蛋白的靶向递送制剂相容。进一步的化学信息学预测强调了全身毒性值以及靶向递送以最小化毒副作用的需求。分子对接和动力学模拟显示，替米沙坦-MyoVc货物结构域复合物在18 ns模拟期间强健且稳定。生物信息学和化学信息学数据支持吡格列酮和替米沙坦作为LUAC的有前景的重新定位药物，突出其亲脂性及与外泌体组分（如白蛋白）的相容性。化学信息学还指出了潜在的脱靶效应和肝毒性，强调了外泌体靶向递送的重要性。分子对接和MD模拟确认了药物-外泌体载体复合物的亲和力和稳定性。所提出的外泌体货物工程，用于将这些药物靶向递送至肺细胞，可能增强NSCLC治疗并解决耐药性问题，同时最小化全身毒性。
